title: Content Plan
subtitle: YouTube only · one long form a week · shorts daily

daily.detail: One is the floor and it is never skipped. Two is the day you should be having. Three only when the bank is deep enough that a third costs you nothing. Never post a third just to hit three.
15 minutes from the Czech screen. Non-negotiable and non-optional, which is exactly why it's small.
Filmed Monday, live Saturday 10am. It is the week's centrepiece and the source of most of the week's shorts.

premise: One platform now: **YouTube**. No Instagram, no cross-posting, no second audience to feed. Everything you make is built for one algorithm and one set of numbers, which means you can actually learn what's working instead of guessing across two.

The shape is a long form a week and shorts every day. The long form is the thing worth making — it's what builds a channel people subscribe to, and it's the only route to watch-hours monetisation. The shorts are reach, and most of them are cut out of the long form you already filmed. One shoot feeds the whole week.

Content history is wiped. This is **Day 1**. The two previous restarts died on a baseline that never got filmed, so the baseline is now the first long form and it goes up this Saturday whether it's good or not.

The brand is unchanged: you're a **test subject**, not a fitness influencer. You put your own body through things and publish the numbers whether they flatter you or not. That's what lets one channel hold a Viking diet, a Navy SEAL fitness test and a sprint transformation without looking scattered.

spine.name: Marathoner to sprinter
spine.why: You ran Gold Coast in July. Every adaptation in your legs is currently wrong for sprinting — slow-twitch dominant, built for economy instead of force. That conflict is the hook, and nobody else can make that video because it's true about you.
spine.targetNote: Fix the number after the baseline, not before. Sub-13 is fit, sub-12 is genuinely top few percent of adult men, sub-11 is club-athlete. Don't say '1%' on camera until you can defend it.

phases.name: Ramp
phases.focus: Tendon and hamstring prep. Nothing maximal until 1 Oct. This gate is the whole plan's insurance policy.
phases.story: Baseline, and 'why I'm not allowed to sprint yet'

phases.name: Power
phases.focus: Heavy lower body, plyos, hill sprints. Bodyweight goes up — that's content, not failure.

phases.name: Speed
phases.focus: Max velocity, flying 30s, mechanics. The first real time drops land here.
phases.story: Clock reveals — the highest-retention thing you own

phases.name: Sharpen & trial
phases.focus: Block starts, race modelling, taper, then the filmed public time trial.
phases.story: The payoff video the whole channel has been pointing at

spine.risk: Sprinting off an endurance base is the highest hamstring-tear risk in athletics. Tear one and the arc dies with your leg. Nothing maximal until 1 Oct — this is the one place impatience costs you everything.

formats.name: The Quest
formats.what: The sprint transformation — training, times, setbacks, the numbers on screen.
formats.why: The spine. It's the only reason anyone subscribes rather than just watching once.

formats.name: Ancient Protocols
formats.what: 24 hours eating and training as a historical warrior culture.
formats.why: Highest reach per hour of effort you own. Weird, searchable, argument-provoking, cheap to film.

formats.name: The Standard
formats.what: Elite, military and historical fitness tests. Pass or fail, on camera.
formats.why: Built-in stakes and a built-in ending — people watch to find out if you make it.

rhythm.note: One shoot day, one edit block, one publish. Shorts are cut on Thursday and scheduled, so the daily post is a tap, not a job. If the shorts bank drops under 7, Monday gets longer — the other days don't.

package: For long form the title and thumbnail exist **before** you film. If you can't write a title someone would click, don't shoot it.
Title states a number and a stake: 'I Ran a Marathon in July. Here's My 100m Time.' No cleverness, no colons full of adjectives.
Thumbnail: one face, one object, one readable word at phone size. Look at it at thumbnail scale before you accept it.
Click-through rate 4–6% is fine at this size, 8%+ is working. Under 3% is a packaging problem, not a content problem — reshoot the thumbnail, not the video.
Average view duration matters more than length. A 9-minute video watched to 5 minutes beats an 18-minute one watched to 4.
hook: First 1.5 seconds decide it. Number + stake + conflict: 'I ran a marathon in July. Today I'm trying to break 12 seconds.'
Cold open on the strangest visual you have. Never open on your face talking.
On-screen text mirrors the spoken hook — most people watch muted.
No 'hey guys', no 'in this video', no intro. On long form the intro is 10 seconds, maximum.
keep: State the open loop in the first 3 seconds, resolve it at the end.
Shorts: cut every 1.5–2.5 seconds, and make the last frame flow back into the first so it loops.
Long form: a new question every 60–90 seconds. Chapters are for you, not the viewer — use them to check you haven't got a flat two minutes.
Keep a number visible — a timer, the scale, the plate count. It's the reason to stay.
Film the failures. They outperform the wins and they make the wins believable.
share: Argument bait: 'Roman soldiers ate better than you do.'
Number every post — 'Day 41 of 150' says there's a story and they've missed some.
Every short ends pointing somewhere: the long form, or the next day's answer.
Let comments pick the next protocol. Ownership converts watchers into subscribers.
One thing they could actually do tomorrow.

watch: Shorts: swipe-away rate in the first 3 seconds. Want 70%+ still there. Below 60% means the hook failed, not the video.
Long form: click-through rate and average view duration, in that order. CTR gets them in, AVD decides whether YouTube shows anyone else.
Subscribers per video — the only number that compounds, and the one the whole long-form strategy exists for.
rules: Any format that hits 3× your baseline: make 3 more within 7 days.
Any format that underperforms 3 times running: drop it, don't fix it.
Never judge a post before 72 hours — shorts spike late and long form spikes later.
Posted weekly at 7/10 beats posted monthly at 9/10. Consistency is the whole game at this stage.
One review, Sunday, ten minutes. Checking the numbers daily is a way of not filming.

money.note: Optimise for reach now; build so the money works later without a jarring pivot.
points: YouTube Partner Program has two doors and the weekly long form puts you in front of both: 1,000 subs + 4,000 public watch hours in 12 months, or 1,000 subs + 10 million shorts views in 90 days.
The long form is the watch-hours route. A 10-minute video watched half through by 1,000 people is ~830 hours — four or five of those get you there. Shorts alone never will.
Long form also earns real ad revenue per view. Shorts pay a fraction of it. The shorts exist to feed the long form an audience.
Pre-workout affiliate isn't live: no brand mentions, and don't sign a competing supplement deal in the meantime.
Show pre-workout unbranded in training footage now, so it reads as continuity later rather than a sellout moment.

notes: The Czech lesson is a daily fixture, not content — but if a day's lesson gives you something genuinely funny or hard, 30 seconds of it is a free short. Optional. Don't let it become a second job.
If a week collapses, the long form is what you protect. Missing a day of shorts costs you a day. Missing the long form costs you the week and the subscribers it would have brought.
Everything published before today is off the board. Day counters, streaks and idea banks all start now.
